title: Schelling segregation dynamics in densely-connected social network graphs
publisher: arXiv (Anastasi & Dalla Riva, University of Canterbury)

key_points.claim: Schelling model run on a dense, non-spatial social network segregates less strongly than sparse networks.
key_points.evidence_quote: a dense social network does not become as strongly segregated as a sparse network

key_points.claim: Agents' same-group neighbour counts closely match desired levels, without the overshoot usually seen in Schelling models.
key_points.evidence_quote: the number of similar neighbours closely matches the agents' desired number, rather than becoming much larger

key_points.claim: Polarisation (measured by embedded dimensionality of a Random Dot Product Graph) needs a much higher same-group preference than earlier Schelling tipping points. Online networks may therefore be structurally harder to polarise.
key_points.evidence_quote: was also much higher than previously observed tipping points in Schelling models

key_points.claim: Group size matters. A moderately small group cannot be polarised, and an extremely small group makes the network unstable.
key_points.evidence_quote: when one group was very small, it was difficult or impossible for the model to stabilise

key_points.claim: Fossett's 'paradox of weak minority preferences' gets mixed support in dense networks.
key_points.evidence_quote: in a dense social network the evidence for the "paradox of weak minority preferences" is mixed

key_points.claim: Asymmetric tolerance raises the tipping point slightly, but a very intolerant group still causes polarisation.
key_points.evidence_quote: polarisation will still occur if one group is very intolerant

key_points.claim: The authors propose extensions: opposite-group preferences, fuzzy group membership, more than two groups.
key_points.evidence_quote: add a desired number of opposite group neighbours, fuzzy set (i.e. continuous) group membership, more than two groups

reliability_notes: Full text was fetched. It is an arXiv preprint and may not be peer reviewed. It covers a narrow topic: Schelling segregation and polarisation on networks. It is only indirectly about artificial societies in general. Simulation-only findings, with no empirical validation.
